audit.whatIsWrong: The chart read Cassiopeia / Skill / Swain / Swain / Cassiopeia / Swain / Swain — Swain favoured in four of seven stages — while every line of prose on the same entry says the opposite: 'the lane flips', 'This is your window', 'You own the straight 1v1 deep into items'. Cassiopeia is at 56.45% over 62 games here.
audit.why: Lane difficulty is a key point and this chart told a player they lose a lane they win.
audit.corrected: Skill / Cassiopeia / Cassiopeia / Cassiopeia / Cassiopeia / Cassiopeia / Skill in both layers — Swain only pulls level with grouped teamfights.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four spikes were listed as Lvl 2-3, Lvl 6, 1st item, then Lvl 1-2 — the last one out of chronological order and duplicating the early-game point, leaving the entry with no late-game spike at all. No cooldown numbers anywhere.
audit.why: Power spikes is a key point; the entry never told you when Swain actually overtakes you, which is grouped teamfights, not a lane level.
audit.corrected: Fourth spike re-pointed to Late and rewritten around Swain's teamfight scaling; Nevermove 12s, Death's Hand 7s to 3s and Demonic Ascension 120s added to the cooldown text.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three separate strings told you to stun Swain 'out of his Demonic Ascension channel'. It is not a channel — Riot's own text describes a transformation that lasts indefinitely while he keeps draining, and the kit carries no channel flag. Nevermove was also called a 'slow, telegraphed ground-target root'; it is a wave that travels out and roots on the way back. Swain's healing was never tied to Grievous Wounds.
audit.why: Point 4 is the most important point. Banking a 120-second ultimate to cancel an ult that cannot be cancelled is the kind of error that loses the fight and the ult, and dodging Nevermove requires knowing the root comes on the return.
audit.corrected: Petrifying Gaze reframed as the tool that breaks his 650 drain radius rather than one that ends his ult; Nevermove's return-trip root stated with its 12s downtime; Ravenous Flock sustain tied to buying Grievous Wounds early.
sources: champ-data/_kits/swain.json (R description, no channel flag; E description 'It then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits'; P Ravenous Flock heal)

edits.before: Petrifying Gaze answers his all-in: if he Nevermove-roots and Demonic Ascension drains on you, point your cone at him to stun him out of the channel and shred him with Twin Fang.
edits.after: Petrifying Gaze answers his all-in: Demonic Ascension is a transformation, not a channel, so the stun will not end it — use it to break his 650 drain radius, then Twin Fang him.

edits.before: His Nevermove (E) root is his only kill setup — a landed E into Vision of Empire (W) bomb and Death's Hand poke is the one window he can blow you up before your poison engine is online.
edits.after: Grouped, Swain pulls level: Death's Hand, a flanking Nevermove pull-root and an indefinite Demonic Ascension win the long fight while you stand squishy with no resistances. Close on your side-lane lead.

edits.before: Hit Level 6 and hold Petrifying Gaze (R) to stun him out of his Demonic Ascension channel if he commits to an all-in
edits.after: Hold Petrifying Gaze (R) for his commit — the stun cannot end Demonic Ascension, but it buys the space to leave its 650 drain

edits.before: Drag you into a sustained fight where his Demonic Ascension (R) drain and soul stacks out-heal your poison damage
edits.after: Drag you into a long fight where Ravenous Flock and the R drain out-heal your poison — buy Grievous Wounds early

edits.before: Level 1 is the real risk: you have one ability and no poison stacking yet, so respect his Death's Hand poke and never stand where his Nevermove (E) can root you into a Vision of Empire (W) bomb — that landed-E window is his only way to blow you up. Once you hit 2-3 and have both Q and Twin Fang, the lane flips: prime him with Noxious Blast (Q), then chain Twin Fang (E) — it refunds most of its cooldown and mana off your own poison, so you out-DPS his Death's Hand poke in any extended trade. His Nevermove is a slow, telegraphed ground-target root; sidestep it with your bonus move speed and the Q speed buff and he has almost no answer to your sustained damage.
edits.after: Level 1 is the real risk: you have one ability and no poison stacking yet, so respect his Death's Hand poke and never stand where his Nevermove (E) can root you into a Vision of Empire (W) bomb — that landed-E window is his only way to blow you up. Once you hit 2-3 and have both Q and Twin Fang, the lane flips: prime him with Noxious Blast (Q), then chain Twin Fang (E) — it refunds most of its cooldown and mana off your own poison, so you out-DPS his Death's Hand poke in any extended trade. Nevermove roots on the return trip, not the throw, so keep moving after the wave passes you and its 12s of downtime is yours.

edits.before: This is your window. With ranks in Q and E you chain near-continuous Twin Fangs, and your boots-free passive move speed plus the Q on-hit speed buff let you weave around his Nevermove so he can never land the root that sets up his combo. At 6, hold Petrifying Gaze: if he roots you and opens Demonic Ascension to drain, turn and point your cone at him to stun him out of the channel, then Twin Fang him down before his soul stacks heal anything back. Lay Miasma (W) on the spot he wants to stand to slow him and tick extra poison — it keeps your Twin Fang refunds rolling even when he tries to walk out of your Q.
edits.after: This is your window. With ranks in Q and E you chain near-continuous Twin Fang casts, and your boots-free passive move speed plus the Q on-hit speed buff let you weave around Nevermove — it roots on the way back, so keep moving after the wave has passed you. At 6, Petrifying Gaze will not end Demonic Ascension, which is a transformation and not a channel; spend the stun and slow to break out of his 650 drain radius, then Twin Fang him down before Ravenous Flock heals it back. Lay Miasma (W) on the spot he wants to stand to slow him and tick extra poison, keeping your Twin Fang refunds rolling.

edits.before: - Swain Demonic Ascension: matchup-defining — His drain mode — disengage and reset the fight when it starts. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your W Miasma like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Swain Demonic Ascension: matchup-defining — 120s, and no stun ends it; break the 650 drain radius. - Nevermove is 12s and roots on the return, not the throw. - Guard your W Miasma like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
